title: Dick Mackey, Wade Schlegel and Fred Waring
summary: Discussion of Dick Mackey's later bands, helping Wade Schlegel (Dave Wade) start out, Wade's career with Waring and a gig story.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well they were already playing horns by the time you were on. Yeah, well Dick Mackey had already left the band. Yeah. What band was Dick Mackey with when he got out of the business?
He had his own band for a long time but I don't know. No, he never had his own band.
He was with, not Harold Kemp, he was with a band from around North Carolina somewhere around that way.

Well he was with Harold Kemp for a while I know because of, I was just talking to his son Sunday when we were talking about that. What? About him being with Harold Kemp, he even recorded with him. Dick did. Dick did, yeah. It was not a very good recording he thought it did.

The sons thought it was fine. Well I know both of Dick's sons, in fact I used one of them for a while there before he left town. He was a drummer he played with, I used him a couple of times. And Dick was responsible for giving Wade Schlegel, did you ever hear Wade Schlegel?

He was responsible for giving him his start with this band. I don't know, I don't think it was Harold Kemp. I think it was another one of these singing bands. But, Wade did give me two pictures of when he was with the Dick Solas and once when he was with Harold Kemp. Wade was very close to me. We corresponded. And then he, I think I told you this, that he came down to his sister's, he came down to his sister's anniversary party. Which he told her that he didn't think he was going to be able to get there. And he surprised her by coming down here. He came out here, changed his clothes and went up to the early nuns club and surprised his sister after he parked the tuxedo on. But Wade passed away not very long ago. And we were very, very close friends in later years. And he was with, he'd tell me different things, he was with Waring quite a while. With Fred Waring, he was strictly a, he was strictly a gag man. He was just dreaming up some gags. We've got a big bundle there. Says what do you guys, what you got there? Says I've got my fireworks. I said you're working. I said you're not having fun over here. Oh yeah, 12 o'clock and we've got to shoot the fireworks. Look I've got my blank pistol. I've got my blank pistol. Used to serve you these 22 blank pistols. And then shoot blanks in them. Come 12 o'clock. Come 12 o'clock he had to go outside and shoot his fireworks. Come 12 o'clock I'm looking for the fiddle player Dave Jacobson. Can't find him anywhere. Next day I said what the hell happened to you Dave? Says I live on Ramport Street. You know what I mean? The 600 block of Ramport Street. He said those niggas down there will take your eye and eat it as a grape. Says I want home. I want to get home before it was too late. He disappeared. So we ended up with the trumpet, saxophone, drums and piano. And it was just a, it was more or less a family affair. I don't think we stayed there until that past one o'clock. But we did make five dollars that night. That was a new price. I think we were still in high school. But Wade was a, Wade was a, there was another trumpet player that, that was from New Orleans who was a very good trumpet player who was a, a Bo, a Boos head. Sterling Boes. Did you ever hear Sterling Boes? Sure. He was with Benny Goodman's band with the, with the drummer. What's, what's the drummer's name? Rupert? No, no. Before that. He was, uh, it was, well, Goodman was with that band. Well, you're not thinking of Wettley or Goodman?
